title: Case Follow-up and Escalation
unit: CS-ICT251101 Monitor and Report Cyber Threats

parts.html:
At the end of this session, you should be able to:

  1. Verify the results of a scan with the customer, client or stakeholder, in plain language (PC 4.1).
  2. Check security solution scan logs for failed actions as per SOP (PC 4.2).
  3. Escalate a failed action to the appropriate authority as per SOP (PC 4.3).
  4. Write a complete escalation record and follow up when there is no response.
  5. Protect personal data and credentials while communicating with stakeholders.

parts.h: 1. A Case Is Not Finished Until …
parts.html: … the person who owns the computer confirms the problem is gone, or someone with the authority to fix it has taken it over. Element 4 of the Competency Standards covers this follow-up: verify the results with the stakeholder, check the scan logs for failed actions, and escalate the failures. In the lab you follow SOC-SOP-05 Case Follow-up and Escalation (~/day9/soc_followup_sop.txt).

parts.h: 2. Verify the Results with the Stakeholder (PC 4.1)
parts.html:
The stakeholder is the customer, client or employee responsible for the affected computer. Find them in the directory and call the directory number (never a number from a suspicious message).

StepWhatExample
TellWhat was found, what the security solution did, what they must do now"We found a trojan in payslip_viewer.exe. The antivirus quarantined it. Please restart your laptop."
AskAre the symptoms gone? Anything unusual?"Do you still see pop-ups or slow performance?"
RecordWho confirmed, when, and what they said"Maria Reyes confirmed at 13:05: laptop normal."
ReplyNext Step (F1.4)
Confirmed resolvedClose the case and record the confirmation
Symptoms remainRe-open the case and re-check the host (Day 8)
No replyTry again after 2 hours; after 2 tries, email the stakeholder's supervisor
NOTE — Talking to stakeholders
Use plain words, not event IDs. Never send or ask for passwords. Share only what the stakeholder needs: a payroll officer does not need the details of another employee's infection (Data Privacy Act, RA 10173).

parts.h: 3. Check the Scan Logs for Failed Actions (PC 4.2)
parts.html:
Event IDFailed ActionExample Cause
1118Remediation action failed (non-critical)File in use by another process
1119Remediation action failed (critical)Access denied
1002Scan stopped before it finishedThe user restarted the PC
1005Scan failedEngine error
2001Security intelligence update failedConnection timed out

Not failures: 1000 scan started, 1001 scan finished, 1116 detected, 1117 action taken, 2000 update succeeded. In the lab: grep -E ",(1118|1119|1002|1005|2001)," ~/day9/scan_logs.csv

The Competency Standards list four appropriate authorities. SOC-SOP-05 says which one receives each failed action. Check the rules in order; the FIRST rule that matches decides.

RuleWhenEscalate ToResponse Target
E1Ransomware or confirmed data loss affecting a Tier 1 assetChief Information Security Officer (CISO)15 min
E2Any other failed action on a red flag or on a Tier 1 assetInformation Security Manager30 min
E3The security solution itself failed (1005, 2001)Security solution vendor (copy the IT Department Manager)Next business day
E4Any other failed action on a business computerIT Department Manager2 hours
TIP — Order matters
FIN-PC-03 is only a Tier 2 workstation, but its ransomware encrypted the Tier 1 FS-01 Finance share, so rule E1 applies (CISO), not E2. A stopped scan is normally E4, but on ENG-PC-11, the source of Day 5's PE infection, it is E2.

The Escalation Record

  • Phone first, then the escalation record by email (~/day9/escalation_template.txt)
  • Ticket, escalated to, rule, time called, host and tier, what failed (event ID and detail)
  • Impact (what is still at risk) and what you need from them (a decision or an action)
  • Response target and the time you will follow up if there is no answer

TermMeaning
StakeholderThe customer, client or employee responsible for the affected system
Case follow-upChecking that the case really ended well, or handing it to someone who can finish it
Failed actionA remediation, scan or update that did not complete
EscalationPassing a problem to a person with more authority or expertise, with all the facts
Appropriate authorityThe role the SOP names for a type of problem (IT manager, information security manager, vendor, CISO)
CISOChief Information Security Officer: the executive responsible for information security
Response targetHow quickly the authority is expected to respond

• TESDA Competency Standards — Cyber Threat Monitoring Level I (ICT Sector), unit CS-ICT251101, Element 4 and Range of Variables 7.
  • NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management (communication and escalation).
  • Microsoft Learn — Microsoft Defender Antivirus event IDs (1000–1119, 2000, 2001).
  • Republic Act No. 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012) and NPC Circular 2016-03 (personal data breach management).
